knowledge_point.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Nonlinear Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u=3{x}^{6}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=18{x}^{5}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (18{x}^{5}) \\  & =18{x}^{5}{e}^{u} \\  & =18{x}^{5}{e}^{3{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-3{x}^{6}-4x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-18{x}^{5}-4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-18{x}^{5}-4) \\  & =(-18{x}^{5}-4){e}^{u} \\  & =(-18{x}^{5}-4){e}^{-3{x}^{6}-4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={((-18{x}^{5}-4){e}^{-3{x}^{6}-4x})|}_{x=-1} \\  & =(-18(-1)^{5}-4){e}^{-3(-1)^{6}-4(-1)} \\  & =14{e}^{1} \\  & =14{e}^{1}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={e}^{-3{x}^{6}-6}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-3{x}^{6}-6.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-18{x}^{5}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot -18{x}^{5} \\  & =-18{x}^{5}\cdot {e}^{u} \\  & =-18{x}^{5}{e}^{-3{x}^{6}-6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={-18{x}^{5}{e}^{-3{x}^{6}-6}|}_{x=-1} \\  & =-18(-1)^{5}{e}^{-3(-1)^{6}-6} \\  & =18\cdot {e}^{-9} \\  & =\frac{18}{e^{9}}\end{aligned}
$$

\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=18{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (18{x}^{2}) \\  & =18{x}^{2}{e}^{u} \\  & =18{x}^{2}{e}^{6{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(18{x}^{2}{e}^{6{x}^{3}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =18(1)^{2}{e}^{6(1)^{3}} \\  & =18{e}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$
